title: Login screen
description: The sign-in screen as the reference composition for a whole screen built from the contract: a stage (chosen 2026-09-25 at /lab/login-2 over a photo panel beside the form, a framed sheet and a dark pane), in parts the route arranges. LoginStage is the bark-100 ground at the viewport's height in three rows; LoginBar holds LoginBrand (the wordmark) and LoginNav (the visitor's actions); LoginCard is the flat Card centred in the middle row, whose header the route fills from Card's own parts (a title, a lede); LoginForm is two required Inputs, a slotted help link and a stacked CardFooter of primary Sign in, an 'or sign in with' rule, the SSO button and a slotted footnote; LoginFooter is one line at the foot. No photograph: flat on flat. One composition for phone and desktop, tightened below 40rem of the stage.

anatomy.description: Root div with data-slot="login-stage": a grid of three rows (auto, 1fr, auto), min-height 100svh, bark-100, 1.25rem 2rem 1rem padding, an inline-size container named login-stage. It owns the ground; the route paints nothing (theming §1.6).
A header with data-slot="login-bar": a flex row, space-between, for LoginBrand on the left and LoginNav on the right.

A span with data-slot="login-brand" that sizes the svg inside it (6.5rem wide, 5.5rem below 40rem) and colours it needle-800 through currentColor. The route imports the wordmark asset and drops it in.
A nav with data-slot="login-nav": a 0.5rem row for the visitor's actions, Buttons asChild around router Links (a discrete link and the one primary of the bar).

The house Card in its flat variant (data-slot="card", data-variant="flat"), centred in the middle row: the width up to 26rem, 1.75rem 2rem padding (1.5rem 1.25rem below 40rem), the xl radius, the bark-200 hairline at 60%. Its module gives the card's header 1.25rem below.
Composed by the route from Card's parts: CardTitle at level 1 (the page's main content) over a one-line CardDescription lede.

react-aria Form with native validation: isRequired blocks the submit, the first empty field takes focus and FieldError shows the message; onSubmit hands the credentials to the caller. Centred at 22rem.

Email Input (type email, autocomplete username, autoFocus) and Password Input (autocomplete current-password), then the slotted helpAction right-aligned beneath them. Nothing user-scoped: which workspaces exist is an answer the API gives after sign-in, so no workspace picker before it (component-architecture §6.4).

Stacked: the primary submit, the 'or sign in with' rule and the secondary Single sign-on button (only with onSingleSignOn), and the footnote (a p at text-sm, bark-500, whose links are needle-800 and answer in bloom on hover).
A p with data-slot="login-footer": one centred line at text-sm, bark-600, in the stage's last row (the copyright, a privacy link, the demo's disclaimer).

usage: A reference composition, not a reusable primitive: copy the structure (a stage in three rows, a flat Card in the middle, the header from Card's parts, the form from Field-composed controls) rather than the components.

The route arranges: <LoginStage><LoginBar><LoginBrand>…</LoginBrand><LoginNav>…</LoginNav></LoginBar><LoginCard><CardHeader>…</CardHeader><LoginForm … /></LoginCard><LoginFooter>…</LoginFooter></LoginStage>. The title, the lede, the bar's actions, the help link, the footnote and the footer are the route's words and links; the route needs no CSS of its own.

Controlled: onSignIn({ email, password }) is all the form reports and the component never navigates; the route decides where a sign-in lands. Ask for nothing user-scoped before sign-in (workspaces, names, plans): the authenticated shell resolves those once it knows who signed in.

Pass onSingleSignOn (no arguments) to render the SSO button; leave it out and the rule goes with it. Pass helpAction and footnote as nodes built from Button asChild and router Links so the router stays in the route.

The card is flat because the ground is flat (theming §4.6): a card separates from bark-100 by tint and hairline. Glass is for a card on a photograph, and this screen has none; the FullBleedCanvas and ImageOverlay stay in the registry for screens that do.
Validation is react-aria's native behaviour; do not add noValidate or an attempted-submit flag. Messages come through errorMessage on each Input.
The alternatives this was chosen from (a photo panel beside the form, a framed sheet, the dark pane) stay at /lab/login-2 as the archive; the first round at /lab/login.
